1. The Dom unlocks and chooses the rules.
2. In Settings → Apps, choose the shared included-app list.
3. Complete Android permission setup; open the Permission setup guide if Accessibility is restricted.
4. On Home, choose the service duration and tap Enter Service.
5. Lock Dom controls and hand over to the Sub. Editing settings or releasing a service lock requires the Dom.

Display over other apps lets SubHub draw censors and safety controls. Accessibility powers App Mode, foreground-app assignment, visible-text geometry, taps, scrolling, and daily limits. Android 13+ notification access keeps protection status visible. Screen Capture is optional and Android asks for MediaProjection approval every session. Hardcore requests Device Admin separately; ordinary censoring never needs it.

The Dom holds the reins: features, rules, apps, service duration, PayPal, arrangements, and safety release. The Sub sees the rules, Wallet balances, and permitted actions. Enter Service and Leave Service control the whole service; feature switches choose what participates. Keep the Dom PIN private. Switching between Dom and Sub does not erase settings or stop an active service.

Enter Service starts the service and its session. Choose 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or Permanent before entering. The duration defines when Leave Service is allowed; Dom can release the lock earlier. After reboot, an active lock can resume App Mode when Android allows it. Screen Capture always needs fresh Android approval.

Settings → Apps has one include/exclude list. Every enabled service feature uses it: Censor, Limits, Subliminal Messaging and Popup Storm. Excluded apps do not participate. The list does not turn features on or change app-specific daily allowances. Existing selections migrate to one combined list; new installations start empty.

Enable Subliminal Messaging and choose its phrases, opacity and timing on Rituals. It uses the same included-app list as the other service features. Accessibility shows one faint, touch-through message at a random safe position and removes it smoothly. Messages do not appear in SubHub, the keyboard, Android Settings or excluded apps. Only aggregate impression counts are stored; message history and screen content are not.

Censor uses on-device detection for visible images and explicit text. Appearance stays independent from detection coverage. Gallery Censor is on Rituals and creates censored copies on this device; originals remain unless deletion is explicitly selected.

Limits shows today’s recorded app usage, a combined daily budget and an allowance for each included app. Use either budget or both; the smaller remaining time applies. Usage resets at local midnight. When a budget is exhausted, SubHub returns the covered app to Home. Removing an app preserves the recorded combined total for that day. SubHub, keyboards and essential Android surfaces are excluded. Accessibility is required; Screen Capture alone cannot enforce foreground-app time.

A little tribute for temptation. Wallet is optional and local until checkout. The Dom chooses enabled events, prices, batching, correction time, and daily and weekly caps. Manual checkout requires the payer to be present. Saved-wallet auto-pay is separate and explicit; it runs only while Wallet, Hardcore Mode, an active service lock, and a verified saved PayPal wallet are all active. PayPal may still decline or ask the payer to authorize again.

Use a PayPal Business account and create or select a REST app in the PayPal Developer Dashboard. Start with Sandbox credentials and a sandbox personal buyer; Live credentials are separate and move real money. Enable Save payment methods/Vault for the same app and complete PayPal’s business-profile eligibility step under Account Settings › Payment Preferences. In Wallet → PayPal with Dom access, choose the matching environment, connect its Client ID and secret, then Link Payer Wallet and approve the billing agreement in PayPal. Linking itself creates no charge. PayPal’s dashboard may label the eligible wallet capability “PayPal and Venmo”; Venmo is US-only and is not a German/EUR payment option.

Hardcore Mode is optional platform-supported friction. It asks for Device Admin, adds a deliberate Dom release before protected uninstall/data-clear paths, and can guard Android settings while service is active. It does not wipe data, set passwords, use the camera, force-lock the device, or make Android unbreakable. Confirm the Dom PIN and recovery path before handing over control.

If censors do not appear, open Permission Check and fix the missing permission. Check the included-app list and the feature settings. If App Mode stalls, turn SubHub off and on in Android Accessibility, then use Leave Service and Enter Service when the service lock allows it. Android secure windows may block capture. Diagnostics shows service state, detector, frame rate, latency, and recent errors. For PayPal, check the selected environment and credentials, and confirm the saved-wallet status is Ready.

Image and text detection run on this device. Ordinary screen snapshots are processed in memory and are not saved. Censor Lab saves a bounded video only after Android’s screen-recording approval, never records microphone audio, and keeps the capture private until you share it. Settings, the included-app list, statistics, arrangements, diagnostics, and Wallet history otherwise stay local unless you export or share them. PayPal credentials and saved-wallet IDs are encrypted with Android Keystore; OAuth, checkout, wallet authorization, and fraud-risk data go directly to PayPal.

Studio creates and edits .sub files in four steps: Details, Features, Images and Review. Start blank or copy the current setup, configure each included setting, add or remove images, then save to the Library or share through Android. Draft edits never change live settings. The Dom reviews selected sections before applying a pack and can restore the previous settings. Packs do not add setting locks; Enter Service and Leave Service remain the master controls. The Dom can explicitly attach merchant details encrypted with a separate passphrase. Share only with trusted recipients: their app can read the secret after unlocking. Payer authorization, verification, payment history, currency and automatic-payment consent stay local. Encrypted merchant updates require restoring the old settings and a fresh Dom review. Security and duration choices are recommendations only: packs never enable Android access, start service, change the Dom PIN or import the included-app list. Old profiles, user backups and .bbpack interfaces are retired; previously saved private files are not automatically deleted.

Open Manage Updates below to check SubHub’s public GitHub releases.
